name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Stanton holds a roughly 4-to-1 fundraising edge with $2 million on hand and no outside spending against him
The district leans Democratic (D+4) and Stanton is an established incumbent
Polymarket prices Stanton's win probability at about 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings exist, leaving the error band wide
model.rationale: Stanton combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and a dominant money advantage over Zuhdi Jasser, while prediction markets price him near certain to win; with no polling contradicting that picture, the seat stays in the Safe D column.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Stanton or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow the margin, though no current signs point that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton seeks another term in a Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $2.1 million and holding $2 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. Polymarket traders give Stanton about a 95 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing. Those signals all point the same direction: a Democratic-held seat with a well-funded incumbent and an underfunded challenger. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the error band wide even though the expected outcome is not close.
